proposal.rationale: Transfer hypothesis: apply the cited packaging-permeability work to the balance between raspberry respiration and gas exchange through the film. Comparing oxygen/carbon-dioxide transmission, measured headspace and spoilage could explain why the current pack fails before the buyer's target. Mixed-berry evidence motivates a raspberry-only experiment; it does not establish 14-day shelf life or the researcher's current laboratory capacity.

facts.quote: Raspberries for Germany arrive with mould on day 9; buyers want 14 days.
Packaging material permeability screening for MAP of mixed-berry trays

plan.question: Joint-project topic: raspberry packaging for a 14-day cold chain. Can film permeability and headspace conditions improve shelf life? A follow-on industrial PhD could model how temperature excursions and harvest-lot variation change the useful permeability range, subject to safe pilot results and supervision/funding agreements.
plan.experiment: Propose an 8-week pilot: randomize trays within three harvest lots to the current pack or three candidate films. Keep fill weight and handling comparable; log temperature and headspace gases. Assess mold, firmness and sensory acceptability on days 0, 7, 9, 12 and 14. A food-science review must set sample sizes and safe sensory-testing rules.
plan.metrics: Proposed gate: a candidate meets buyer-agreed mold, firmness and sensory criteria on day 14 in all pilot lots, without unsafe gas conditions. Report lot-level uncertainty and cost per pack. Day 14 is a target to test, never an outcome guaranteed by prior work.
plan.companyAsk: Request sample fruit, current packaging specifications, cold-chain logs and a quality contact. Confirm access to storage and measurements, and cap the sample and consumables budget before the first lot.
plan.researcherAsk: Invite the researcher to select permeability ranges, design randomized comparisons and analyze lot variation. Ask company quality staff to document handling and buyer rejection criteria. Confirm personal contribution, measurement access and availability; no lab or supervision commitment is assumed.
plan.milestones: Weeks 1–2: buyer acceptance criteria, film sourcing and protocol. Weeks 3–6: three staggered lot trials with temperature logging. Week 7: uncertainty and cost analysis. Week 8: packaging recommendation or documented no-go.
plan.risks: Mixed-berry results may not transfer to raspberry-only packs or fluctuating transport temperatures. Anaerobic conditions and sensory rejection can defeat longer shelf life. Do not release experimental packs for sale without the appropriate safety review.
plan.meeting: Before a 45-minute meeting, request current film specifications and one approved rejected-shipment temperature log. Quality manager and researcher agree buyer thresholds, harvest windows and who can measure gases and microbiology. Leave with a sampling plan and a dated safety/access/budget decision before sourcing films.
plan.terms: Propose a capped trial budget, company ownership of shipment records, agreed access to de-identified measurements, negotiated foreground IP and a 60-day publication review. No funding or participation is secured.
